 Home » Business »  Economy Gold Falls Rs 1,877, Silver Slumps Rs 6,567 In Futures Trade
 Economy DC Correspondent 16 Nov 2026 12:24 PM IST 16 Nov 2026 12:24 PM IST Weak spot demand and selling pressure weigh on precious metals; global gold and silver prices also decline
 x As Preferred
Source Gold and silver prices declined in futures trade on Monday, with gold falling Rs 1,877 to Rs 1,34,828 per 10 grams and silver slumping Rs 6,567 to Rs 1,69,742 per kg amid weak demand and selling pressure.
 On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), gold contracts for December delivery traded lower by Rs 1,877, or 1.37 per cent, at Rs 1,34,828 per 10 grams in a business turnover of 15,567 lots.
 Silver contracts for December delivery declined by Rs 6,567, or 2.19 per cent, to Rs 1,69,742 per kg in a business turnover of 17,090 lots. Analysts attributed the decline in gold prices to weaker spot demand, while selling by market participants mainly weighed on silver prices.
 Globally, gold futures declined by 0.64 per cent to USD 3,861.35 per ounce, while silver was trading 3.59 per cent lower at USD 47.36 per ounce in New York.
